The head of the Department of Justice, also known as the attorney general. C. The head of the Supreme Court who presides over conferences and assigns opinions. D. The chair of the Senate Judiciary Committee.
questions_and_answers.answer: Final Answer: The solicitor general is the top attorney representing the federal government before the Supreme Court. They select which cases to pursue on behalf of the government and have a significant influence on the Court's decisions. Often referred to as the "10th Justice", their opinions are highly regarded by the justices. ; Explanation: Who is the Solicitor General? The solicitor general is the top lawyer who represents the federal government in cases argued before the Supreme Court. He or she plays a critical role in determining which cases the government will appeal from lower courts and in deciding the government’s position in those cases. The solicitor general is responsible for preparing and submitting briefs and presenting oral arguments during the hearings. Approximately two-thirds of all Supreme Court cases involve the federal government, underscoring the solicitor general's significance in the judicial process.
